rendered:
The paper gives limonene and nerolidol titers in several places. The values fall into separate sets that do not match.

A. Section 4.3[1], opening sentence (carried over the page break): limonene and nerolidol reach 14.12[2] g/L and 32.33[3] g/L, respectively, "in 5-L bioreactors[4]", after the shake-flask sentence citing [16][5]. The sentence does not say which strain these values come from.

B. Introduction: maximum nerolidol titer "Maximum titers of 70.50[6]" g/L.

C. Section 4.3[7], later paragraph: "limonene reached 22.8[8]" g/L, labelled the highest reported [21][9]. "(E)-Nerolidol reached 70.50[10]" g/L, cited [24][11].

D. Table 2[12]: (S)-limonene 22,800[13] mg/L (strain HBQA7 → LSF6, fed-batch, 100[14] h, ref. [21][15]); (E)-nerolidol 70,500[16] mg/L (strain HBQA7 → LN62, fed-batch, 96[17] h, ref. [24][18]).

Consistency: the maximum values agree across the introduction, Section 4.3[19], and the table. Limonene at 22,800[20] mg/L is the same value as 22.8[21] g/L, and nerolidol at 70,500[22] mg/L matches 70.50[23] g/L once the units are converted. The same references are cited for each maximum in the text and the table.

The exception is the first set of values in Section 4.3[24] (item A above). Those values, 14.12[25] and 32.33[26] g/L, do not appear in the table or anywhere else in the document, and the text does not identify their strain or study. They are lower than the maxima, which is not contradictory if they describe a different strain or condition, but the paper does not reconcile them with the maxima quoted above.

Not a contradiction, different strains and studies.
